newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer but negative bias remains.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer but negative bias remains.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Friday but dealers said the currency was still carrying a slightly negative bias and saw it testing slowly lower.
One dealer said the Kiwi had firmed after running into a range of buyers around US$0.6915.
"There were a number of people who had shorted the Kiwi, expecting it to come off because the Aussie had come off overnight," he said.
"So those guys were just looking to take their shorts back around the 0.6915 level."
The Kiwi closed at 0.6928/35 and at 68.39 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6914/21 and 68.04 at the open.
But rising New Zealand bond yields and the failure of the Australian unit to recover from its recent weakness did not augur well for the Kiwi.
"I think the overall bias is still a little negative, given the way the bond market has performed over the last few days and given the way the Aussie is," a trader said.
The New Zealand currency was seen trading in a 0.6910-40 range overnight.
